introHeading: The studio booth for Queens weddings, catering halls and family celebrations
introParas: Queens throws the biggest guest lists we cover all year, and a lot of that is multigenerational — three, sometimes four generations in the same catering hall in Astoria or Flushing. The studio booth's controlled lighting is what makes it work at that scale: a proper portrait setup that flatters grandparents and toddlers under the same settings, rather than a phone flash that only works for whoever's standing closest.

Catering halls also tend to run big rooms with house lighting built for a DJ, not a camera — dim, colored, constantly shifting. Our lighting rig overrides that entirely, so portraits taken late in the reception under a moving light show look the same as the ones taken at cocktail hour. It is also increasingly the booth requested by Long Island City offices, where creative and tech companies use it for headshot days that double as a team event.

We ask for a 10ft x 10ft footprint where the hall allows it — most Queens catering halls have room to spare — or 8ft x 8ft if the space is tighter, plus a 110V outlet within 15 feet that isn't already feeding the DJ booth. Given how large these events run, we often recommend pairing the studio booth with a second, faster-moving booth like the roamer so a long guest list never turns into a long line.

faqHeading: Studio Photo Booth in Queens — FAQ

faqs.q: Is the studio booth good for large, multigenerational family portraits?
faqs.a: It's one of the main reasons Queens weddings and Sweet Sixteens book it. The lighting is controlled and consistent, so a portrait of the whole extended family looks as clean as one of just the couple — no relying on the venue's house lighting to flatter everyone evenly.

faqs.q: Our catering hall has colored DJ lighting on the dance floor — will that affect the portraits?
faqs.a: No. The studio booth brings its own lighting setup, which overrides whatever the room is doing. Portraits taken late into a Queens reception look the same as the ones taken during cocktail hour.

faqs.q: Can the studio booth handle a large guest count without a long line?
faqs.a: It's built for portrait quality more than raw speed, so for the biggest Astoria and Flushing guest lists we often recommend pairing it with a second station, like the roaming booth, so seated tables and the dance floor both get covered without a bottleneck.

faqs.q: Is the studio booth used for corporate headshots in Long Island City?
faqs.a: Yes — it's become a regular request from LIC offices running headshot days alongside a team event. The DSLR and lighting produce usable headshots delivered by email on the spot.

faqs.q: How much space does the studio booth need in a catering hall?
faqs.a: 10ft x 10ft is optimal, and most Queens catering halls have that to spare. We can compress to 8ft x 8ft with 7.5ft of ceiling clearance if needed.

faqs.q: Is there a travel fee for a studio booth rental in Queens?
faqs.a: Queens is a standard service area with no surprise fees. We quote travel from your venue ZIP code before you book.

faqs.q: Do you carry insurance and can you provide a COI for a Queens catering hall?
faqs.a: Yes. We carry a $3 million liability insurance policy. If your venue needs a certificate of insurance naming them as additionally insured, reply to your booking confirmation with their contact email and we'll send it over.
About 20 minutes once we're in the room. We arrive a full hour before your scheduled start so the lighting is tested before guests arrive; idle time before that is $150 per hour.

faqs.q: Is the studio booth a good option for quinceañera portraits?
faqs.a: Yes. The controlled lighting produces the same clean, editorial-style portrait for the honoree, her court and the extended family that we deliver at weddings and Sweet Sixteens, regardless of the venue's own house lighting.

faqs.q: Is parking easy for guests at our catering hall?
faqs.a: Larger halls in Astoria and Flushing generally have their own guest lots. If your event is in a Long Island City space, street parking or ride-share is more typical, and we plan our own load-in around it.
